reading: Summer wildfires caused a lot of damage.
Scientists say the damage is much bigger than what people can see.
Fires burned about 2,760 acres in north Wales.
People often see black plants, but the real problem is under the ground.
This soil is like a sponge for water and helps store carbon.
Losing the soil makes climate change worse and the land weaker.
This important soil can take thousands of years to grow again.
Scientists are collecting soil samples to study the damage.

vocabulary.definition: large fires that burn in forests or natural areas, often out of control.
made something happen or created a result.
harm or hurt to something, making it less good or useful.
people who study nature and the world to understand how things work.
something that is difficult or causes trouble.
the top layer of earth where plants grow.
bringing things together, often to keep or study them.

entries.ja: 森林や自然の地域で燃え広がり、しばしば制御できない大規模な火事。
entries.ko: 숲이나 자연 지역에서 타오르며, 종종 통제할 수 없는 큰불.
entries.zh-Hans: 在森林或自然区域燃烧的大火，通常难以控制。
entries.es: Incendios grandes que queman en bosques o áreas naturales, a menudo sin control.
entries.pt-BR: Grandes incêndios que queimam em florestas ou áreas naturais, muitas vezes fora de controle.

entries.ja: 何かを引き起こしたり、結果を生み出したりした。

entries.pt-BR: Fez com que algo acontecesse ou criou um resultado.

entries.pt-BR: Dano ou prejuízo a algo, tornando-o menos bom ou útil.

entries.es: Personas que estudian la naturaleza y el mundo para entender cómo funcionan las cosas.

entries.pt-BR: Algo que é difícil ou causa problemas.

entries.ja: 植物が育つ地球の表層。

entries.pt-BR: A camada superior da terra onde as plantas crescem.

entries.ja: 何かを保管したり研究したりするために、物を一緒に集めること。
